description: Code that runs because a module is loaded, not because a symbol is used: top-level statements, effectful initializers, and every module behind a barrel. A file that loads a module depends on its evaluation, whether or not it uses an import. Function-body changes keep symbol-level precision.

scenarios.name: top-level-side-effect-change
scenarios.description: setup.ts registers a handler at load time. app.test imports `helper` but never uses it; indirect.test loads setup through boot.ts; types.test uses a type from setup, which depends on its module scope.

scenarios.name: effectful-initializer-change
scenarios.description: `export const plugin = register('logger')` runs when config.ts loads. config.test never uses `plugin`, but loads config.ts.

scenarios.name: side-effect-behind-a-barrel
scenarios.description: barrel.test imports only `a` from lib/index.ts, but loading the barrel loads b.ts, whose top-level code changed.

scenarios.name: function-body-behind-a-barrel
scenarios.description: Changing b()'s body doesn't change what loading b.ts does: symbol level still skips barrel.test, which uses only `a`.

scenarios.name: function-body-of-an-unused-import
scenarios.description: Nobody calls helper(): its body changing affects no test at symbol level, although three tests load setup.ts.
